text:
maria: quick heads up — noticed tokens/sec drop on prod batch jobs after switching to flash_v2 for long sequences (>4096). throughput down ~18% on p4d runs. anyone else seeing this?

sam: saw a blip last night, didn't dig in. can you paste profiler output?

maria: pasted below from our lightweight tracer (avg over 100 requests):

```
Kernel breakdown (flash_v2, seq=4096, bs=8):
- flash_attn_forward: 9.8 ms (72%)
- kv_paged_copy: 2.6 ms (19%)
- cuda_memcpy_async: 0.9 ms (7%)
- other: 0.4 ms (2%)
Total p99 latency per token chunk: 13.7 ms
tokens/sec (observed): ~880
```

maria: quick cost calc: p4d @ $3.20/hr (spot avg). at 880 tokens/sec => 3.168M tokens/hr => $3.20 / 3.168 = $1.01 per M tokens. that's much worse than previous paged+fused baseline which was ~ $0.82/M.

devin: interesting. on my laptop sim I saw flash_v2 win for seq<=2048 but degrade beyond that — kernel memory pressure seems to trigger extra copies. could be our kv-paged interaction.

lee: any chance batching heuristics changed? continuous batching window or max_batch_size? those affect kernel shapes.

maria: we use window_ms=8, max_batch_tokens=65536. didn't change. only swapped attention kernel.

sam: two angles: kernel choice + kv layout. flash_v2 expects contiguous KV slices to avoid extra memcpy. our paged-kv stores blocks that require coalescing for long seqs. profiler shows the 2.6ms paged_copy step grows with seq length.

devin: posted a short repro script in #eng-ml earlier — but quick test suggestion: try flash_v1 or fused_attention for seq=4096 and compare kernel copy times. also try increasing kv_block_size from 64->128 to reduce number of pages.

maria: ran quick A/B:
```
seq=4096, bs=8
- flash_v2: tokens/sec=880, p99 kernel_copy=2.6ms
- fused_attn: tokens/sec=1020, p99 kernel_copy=0.7ms
- flash_v1: tokens/sec=950, p99 kernel_copy=1.1ms
```

maria: dollar math: using same p4d $3.20/hr
```
- flash_v2 -> $1.01 / M tokens
- fused_attn -> $0.87 / M tokens
- flash_v1 -> $0.91 / M tokens
```

lee: so fused_attn gives best $/M for long seqs here. surprised — thought flash_v2 would be best everywhere.

sam: flash_v2 has micro-optimizations that assume large contiguous KV; when we page, overhead kills perf. two paths forward: adapt kernel selection to data layout OR change paged-KV layout for better coalescing. runtime could switch to fused_attn when seq>2048 and kv_page_count>8.

devin: +1 for adaptive selection. we already collect sequence histograms and kv_page counts per request in the router. cheap rule: if estimated memcpy > X ms then choose fused. need to quantify X.

maria: also flag: when we enable continuous prefix caching, hit rate reduces server work but increases average seq length because we replay longer contexts. that pushes us into the regime where flash_v2 loses. put another way: caching improves latency but can regress $/M unless kernel selection adapts.

sam: can we sketch a quick rule of thumb for the console to surface? e.g., "Recommended kernel: fused for avg_seq >= 3072 OR kv_pages >= 6". we can tune thresholds after collecting perf traces for a few hours.

lee: I'll add a lightweight metric in the console: per-model avg_seq and kv_page_histogram + per-kernel tokens/sec counter. should make A/B and rollouts easier.

maria: created a small experiment plan:
- run 4-hour perf trace on canary pool with three kernel variants (flash_v2, flash_v1, fused)
- collect tokens/sec, kernel_breakdown, memcpy_ms, cost $/M tokens
- feed into optimizer for automatic kernel selector rule

Anyone want to own the run/setup?

devin: I'll spin up the canary, add config flags and collect traces. need to patch runtime to log kv_page_count per request.

sam: I'll write the cost aggregation dashboard widget and add a quick alert if $/M increases >10% vs baseline.

maria: perfect. assigning: devin (canary + logging), lee (console metrics), sam (dashboard + alert). I'll follow up with the experiment config and the initial thresholds.

perf-bot: experiment created: exp-2026-03-17-flash-kernel-audit, canary pool p4d-3, retention 72h.

maria: thanks all. goal: keep hosted $/M < $0.90 for long-seq workloads, and ensure kernel selector flips automatically when it's cheaper. will post results in ~6h. :rocket:
